note: Highest leverage in this set: one lever design serves every subject's closing check. Modes are Bloom tiers (recall 1.5, apply 3.0, analyze 4.5, evaluate 6.0) and all four share the same item kinds, so levers are designed per ITEM KIND, not per mode. The lever mechanism (pull_lever, levers on attempts, practice item, observerLever) is built; KC declares none. Two blockers for closed-set levers: (a) generated options carry no near/far or misconception tag (the miss fn says so), so 'far distractor' is only computable for numeric options; (b) a simplify lever on a single MC item cannot 'return to the full item' without the answer being known, so on-item elimination must be recorded as an assisted attempt (S4) and needs a user ruling on R4 for closed-set items.

help.does: Enlarges and outlines the item's own inset/visual (number line, picture key, table, passage excerpt) and publishes its facts so the tutor can read it aloud. Offered only when the item has an inset or visual.
help.carrier: both (shown; tutor reads the inset facts for pre-readers)
help.leak: Only re-shows what the item already renders; code runs findInsetAnswerLeaks on MC/TF insets too (today it runs only for production kinds) and withholds the lever when the inset marks the answer (e.g. a number-line point labelled with the key). Never outlines or colors an option.

help.does: Shows each option's emoji beside its words (the K picture surface) for a grade-1+ learner whose miss suggests a decoding failure.
help.leak: Every option gets its picture or none does; code requires emoji on all options. Pictures are generated per option, so a picture that depicts the key more literally than the foils is a content risk: needs an oracle check.

simplify.does: Greys out and disables one distractor the learner has not picked: the farthest one (numeric: largest |value - key|; text: needs a generator field). The item stays; the next answer is recorded with the lever.
simplify.risk: R4/R3: this is on-item elimination, not a separate simpler item, so the full item cannot return unassisted. Needs a ruling: treat it as assisted work (S4, no first-response credit) rather than a practice item. Leak rule in code: after removal, at least two live options must remain counting the learner's own wrong picks as removed; never offered on a 2-option menu or a match bank's final ask. Text options need a new schema field (per-option far/near tag) because the options record no reason for being wrong.

Spoken kinds need Part B spoken miss names (e.g. named_distractor) before the observer can route by miss; until then nextLever falls back to help-before-simplify.
